prompt:
A full-length figure of an enemy for the pre-fight screen of a mythology card game, made by hand like a 1993 fantasy trading-card or game-book illustration, exactly matching the game's painted backgrounds: bold, wobbly black pen-and-ink outlines around every shape, filled with thin, flat, transparent watercolour and gouache washes. Big simple flat shapes of colour with almost no shading or modelling, a little ink cross-hatching in the shadows, blotchy uneven washes with hard dried edges, splatters and visible brush marks, and the rough off-white paper texture and grain showing through the paint. Naive, slightly clumsy, decorative and stylised, like an old printed card with slightly faded, misregistered colour, in the limited palette given below. Absolutely not realistic: no realistic lighting or anatomy rendering, no glossy highlights, no glow, no soft gradients, no fine fur or skin detail, no oil-painting look, no 3D, no digital painting, not modern concept art or AI art. Seen in three-quarter view from slightly below, turned partly away and caught mid-action in a dramatic, dynamic pose: never standing straight, never facing the viewer head-on like an avatar. Give it real depth and volume: overlapping forms, foreshortening, and shading washes and ink hatching that model the body in light and shadow, lit by the light of its scene (given below), as if painted into the same picture as the backdrop; still hand-drawn, never glossy, airbrushed or rendered. A soft, semi-transparent painted shadow on the ground under the feet and a few wisps of the scene's own atmosphere (smoke, mist or embers) around the lower legs, so the figure sits in the scene. The whole figure fits inside the frame. Cut out cleanly on a fully transparent background apart from that shadow and those wisps: no scenery, no frame, no text.

Subject: Polyphemus the Cyclops of Homer's Odyssey: a towering, hairy shepherd giant with a single huge glaring eye in the middle of his brow, wild black beard, a sheepskin over his shoulders, striding out of the shadows with the olive-trunk club swung back over his shoulder and one huge hand reaching forward, a ram shying away at his feet, roaring. Greek in every detail. Light: the red glow of the hearth fire from the lower left.
Colour: near-black browns and deep rust (#1a0b07 to #6b2a14) with ember-orange accents.
